explanation:
Read-only semantic review completed for all 16 cases and 49 exported surfaces (48 EN, 1 RO), covering 14 source facts from the three exact Normans paragraphs p0, p1 and p3; the generator, exported JSONL and provenance were inspected, with two read-only scout checks of the exported row slices. The enumerated answers and statuses are consistent with the declared bounded ontology, but two English paraphrases overstate their source and the Romanian target has an output-language mismatch, so this is not an unconditional semantic approval. This was an independent LLM judgment, not a gold-execution score.

Case-level judgments — IDs below share the prefix source-reference-v1-:
• region: SUPPORTED → france; region-to-country direction is correct, and all three questions preserve it.
• name-giver: SUPPORTED → normans for the source's eponym relationship; en-1/en-2 are faithful, but en-3 adds an intentional self-naming act not established by the passage (finding 1).
• raider-origins: SUPPORTED → denmark, iceland, norway; all three explicitly enumerated origins are returned without treating the list as an explicit denial of other origins.
• leader: SUPPORTED → rollo; the antecedent of 'their leader' is the Norse raiders and pirates, not their Norman descendants.
• fealty: SUPPORTED → charles_iii under the predicate's explicit meaning 'agreed to swear'; the three positive surfaces preserve agreement/promised fealty rather than claiming a completed oath. The predicate name/alias 'swore fealty to' is less precise than that declared meaning.
• leader-fealty-join: SUPPORTED → norse_raiders; both clauses bind the same group, not Rollo personally and not the Normans as a substituted descendant group.
• leader-reversed: UNKNOWN, empty tuples; Charles III's role as recipient of promised fealty does not establish that any group had him as its leader, and no explicit leadership denial is present.
• fealty-reversed: UNKNOWN, empty tuples under the agreement relation; the passage does not establish Rollo as recipient. en-1 switches to a completed oath and needs correction (finding 2); en-2/en-3 preserve the intended recipient contrast.
• region-polarity: REFUTED, empty tuples; the explicit positive region_in(normandy, france) opposes the ground negative query, unlike mere absence of support.
• absence-not-negation: UNKNOWN, empty tuples; neither raiders_from(norse_raiders, france) nor its explicit negation is present. Listing Denmark, Iceland and Norway does not supply hard negative evidence about France.
• adopted-language: SUPPORTED → gallo_romance; 'They' refers to the Normans. No substitution of generic 'Roman language' or of the subsequently named Norman dialect is made.
• sicily-founder: SUPPORTED → roger_ii through founded_under; the target and surfaces preserve 'Norman adventurers ... under Roger II' rather than asserting that Roger acted alone.
• antioch-founder: SUPPORTED → bohemond_i; direct person-to-polity founding attribution is explicit.
• duchy-treaty: SUPPORTED → treaty_saint_clair; the treaty establishes the duchy, without extracting an exact founding instant from its beginning as a fiefdom in 911.
• treaty-parties: SUPPORTED → charles_iii, rollo; all three English questions and the Romanian question identify the same two named parties. Romanian question semantics are stable, but its output target is English (finding 3).
• duchy-location: SUPPORTED → neustria; the historical 'former Frankish kingdom' scope is retained, without a present-day location claim.
These annotations comprise 12 supported cases, 3 unknown cases and 1 refuted case: respectively 37, 9 and 3 surfaces, including the Romanian anchor.

Oracle and dispatch: no answer(question_id, answer) relation or upstream answer-span lookup appears in the builder or target circuits. The builder supplies relational facts, typed predicates and query→solve→cnl targets; expected tuples are separately enumerated constants, and original question IDs serve as provenance only. Reading code can establish that separation, but cannot independently prove the historical authorship process claimed by generation_trace. Several short fact quotes require ordinary antecedent resolution from the attached full paragraph; they are contextually entailed, not all standalone subject-complete quotations. The evaluator consumes ontology_sop and setup_sop, routes input_mode=query_only through the guarded runtime, and checks expected tuples/status; the signed reasoner distinguishes explicit opposing evidence from absence. The validator's separate gold-validation predictor is a runtime consistency check, not independent semantic evidence, and was not run here.

Rights and boundary: the recorded primary evidence URL, https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/, explicitly identifies the downloadable dataset as CC BY-SA 4.0 and links dev-v2.0.json; the license record and exported provenance identify SQuAD, Rajpurkar/Jia/Liang, the source URL, the claimed raw hash, derivative modifications/LLM authorship and the same license. This supports the recorded attribution basis, not a legal compliance guarantee. The source is the public upstream development set, not SQuAD's hidden test set; the local 'test' designation is a ChatSOP evaluation boundary. Export metadata prohibits training/checkpoint selection, the export is separate from training data, and the inspected training/selection consumers use explicitly selected formalizer/verbalizer train/dev files, not this suite. No inclusion path was found in those consumers; the flags themselves are declarations, not universal protection against copying or prior pretrained exposure. Hash values were read, not independently recomputed.

Provenance and limits: reviewer is the OMP SourceSemanticAudit harness LLM, assisted by the read-only ExportWorldZero and ExportWorldOneThree scouts, not a human. Harness configuration reports openai-codex/gpt-6-astra; actual backend/provider/model-version/weights identity remains unverified. No files were changed; no tests, builds, GPU work, training, model inference benchmark, or gold execution was performed. Scoped staged and unstaged git diffs were empty, so findings are anchored to the supplied audit snapshot rather than an independently established commit delta.

findings.title: Preserve the eponym relationship in the third naming paraphrase
findings.body: source-reference-v1-name-giver-en-3 asks who 'named the region of Normandy after themselves', whereas the source says that the Normans 'gave their name to Normandy'. The latter establishes the people after whom the region was named, not that those people deliberately performed the naming themselves. This surface therefore introduces an unsupported agentive premise while sharing the same target and gold as the two faithful eponym questions. Replace it with 'After which people was the region of Normandy named, according to the passage?' and update the sealed export/provenance through the project's approved revision process.

findings.title: Keep the reversed-fealty question about an agreement to swear
findings.body: source-reference-v1-fealty-reversed-en-1 asks which group 'swore fealty to Rollo', but swore_fealty_to is explicitly defined as agreement to swear and the passage only attests an agreement. The target therefore asks about a promised oath while this surface asks about an accomplished oath. Both happen to be unknown for Rollo in this fixture, so matching empty gold tuples would conceal the semantic mismatch. Change the surface to 'Which group does the passage say agreed to swear fealty to Rollo?' so the negative contrast changes only the recipient, not the modality.

findings.title: Align the Romanian anchor's output language with its context
findings.body: source-reference-v1-treaty-parties-ro-1 has language='ro' in both the row and model-facing context, but the target is created before the surface loop and hardcodes 'language en'. The runtime's cnl dispatch honors that explicit field, so the Romanian anchor's gold response is English; a model emitting the natural Romanian CNL target also loses canonical-match credit, even though the execution signature ignores CNL language. Generate the CNL language per surface and adjust same-case target comparison to permit that presentation-only difference, or explicitly supply a fixed-English output-language contract if that is the intended task.
